summary:
X-TRACKER transforms NASA’s SPHEREx near-infrared sky surveys into an immersive, spaceship-cockpit web experience designed for teachers, students, families, and citizen scientists. Unlike traditional astronomical tools that feel overly technical and intimidating, we built an intuitive, game-like interface where anyone can pilot through space by entering coordinates (RA/Dec), adjusting the Field of View (FOV), or sharing exact sky views via URL parameters.
To tackle the challenge of exploring SPHEREx’s 102 infrared bands across billions of objects, X-TRACKER features an interactive spectral slider alongside one-click molecular filters for \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) (water), \(\text{CH}_{4}\) (methane), and cosmic dust. Users can play time-lapse sequences across multiple epochs to track variable stars like RW Aurigae and R Draconis, or activate Discovery Mode to visually highlight subtle celestial motions and brightness changes.
X-TRACKER is important because scientific discovery thrives when complex data becomes accessible and exciting. By turning overwhelming multi-epoch archives into an engaging, user-friendly exploration tool, we empower classrooms and curious minds worldwide to participate in discovering new planets, brown dwarfs, and comets.
details:
What X-TRACKER Does & How It Works

X-TRACKER is a web-based space exploration tool designed to look and feel like a real spaceship cockpit. Instead of staring at boring tables or complicated scientific software, users can pilot through NASA’s SPHEREx near-infrared sky surveys right from their browser.

• Easy Sky Navigation: Users can pick famous targets from a dropdown list (like RW Aurigae, R Draconis, Barnard’s Star, or WISE 0855) or enter custom Right Ascension (RA), Declination (Dec), and Field of View (FOV) values.

• 102 Infrared Bands & Molecular Filters: A smooth slider lets users scan through all 102 infrared bands (from 0.77 µm to 4.40 µm). We also added instant shortcut buttons for H2O (water), CH4 (methane), and Dust so anyone can see how the sky looks in specific chemical wavelengths.

• Time-Lapse & Discovery Mode: Users can play animations across different years and epochs (combining SPHEREx with DSS2, AllWISE, and NEOWISE data) to watch stars change brightness or move. Turning on Discovery Mode highlights differences in glowing red and green colors, making moving objects jump right off the screen.

• Full-Screen & Shareable Links: With one click on Expand View, the cockpit switches to a clean full-screen telescope view. Users can also hit Share to copy a direct link with exact coordinates (?ra=...&dec=...&fov=...) to send to friends or embed in websites.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Our main goal is to make space discovery fun and accessible for everyone—teachers, students, families, and curious beginners. By removing the steep learning curve of traditional astronomy tools, X-TRACKER turns classrooms and living rooms into active space research stations. Anyone can help spot comets, asteroids, brown dwarfs, and potential new planets without needing a degree in astrophysics.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

Most astronomical websites feel outdated and intimidating for everyday people. We wanted to change that by prioritizing User Experience (UX), visual excitement, and simplicity. Designing the interface as an interactive spaceship bridge keeps users engaged, while clear controls ensure that a 10-year-old student and a professional researcher can both use it effortlessly. We also built the system using URL parameters so it is fast, lightweight, and easy to update with new SPHEREx data releases.

Tools & Technologies Used

• Frontend Development: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (built in Visual Studio Code) to create the responsive spaceship cockpit UI, interactive sliders, and smooth visual transitions.

• Live Astronomical APIs & Data Fetching: Integrated direct API connections to fetch real-time sky survey imagery and multi-epoch astronomical datasets (such as DSS2, AllWISE, NEOWISE, and SPHEREx near-infrared concepts) dynamically based on user-selected coordinates (RA, Dec, and FOV). This ensures the platform stays lightweight, fast, and automatically ready for future SPHEREx data releases.
